subject: Biology
central_question: What principles, molecular tools and ordered processes allow scientists to construct, clone, express and recover recombinant DNA products?
in_scope_units: Definition and core principles of modern biotechnology: genetic engineering and bioprocess engineering.
Construction of recombinant DNA and the roles of plasmids, restriction enzymes and ligase.
Restriction enzymes, palindromic sites, sticky ends and gel electrophoresis.
Cloning vectors, origin of replication, selectable markers, cloning sites and insertional inactivation.
Plant and animal vectors and methods for making host cells competent.
Isolation, cutting, amplification, ligation and insertion of recombinant DNA.
Expression of foreign genes, bioreactors and downstream processing.
banned_topics: Detailed agricultural and medical applications that belong to Biotechnology and its Applications.
Detailed Mendelian inheritance and gene-expression regulation outside the recombinant-DNA process.
Unspecified laboratory protocols or reagent concentrations not given in the chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: A foreign DNA fragment automatically multiplies after entering any cell.
known_pitfalls.correction: It must be linked to an origin of replication or integrated into replicating host DNA to be inherited and amplified.

known_pitfalls.claim: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at random.
known_pitfalls.correction: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific sequences, often palindromic, and cut at defined positions.

known_pitfalls.claim: Larger DNA fragments move farther in agarose gel.
known_pitfalls.correction: Smaller negatively charged DNA fragments move farther through the gel toward the anode.
Transformation shows DNA uptake; selectable markers and insertional inactivation are used to distinguish recombinants from non-recombinants.

known_pitfalls.claim: PCR uses ordinary DNA polymerase that is destroyed in every denaturation step.
known_pitfalls.correction: PCR uses a thermostable polymerase such as that from Thermus aquaticus so repeated high-temperature cycles are possible.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Exercise 2 to diagram restriction-enzyme action on a recognition site.
Use NCERT Exercise 7 to construct and verify palindromic DNA sequences.
Use NCERT Exercise 9 to explain reporter enzymes and insertional inactivation.
Use NCERT Exercise 10 to define origin of replication, bioreactors and downstream processing.
Finish with NCERT Exercise 11 to explain PCR, restriction enzymes and chitinase.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises are numbered 1 to 12 and cover recombinant proteins, restriction enzymes, palindromes, vectors, PCR, bioreactors and downstream processing.
